key_insight: In strongly stratified flows with no initial vertical shear, horizontal shear instabilities inevitably generate vertical shear and can trigger diapycnal mixing through two distinct routes: direct KH breakdown or a longer nonlinear vortex-mediated pathway.
engineering_relevance: This identifies when and how horizontally sheared stratified flows can produce mixing, helping inform ocean, atmospheric, and geophysical flow models that need accurate subgrid turbulence and transport predictions.
method: Linear stability analysis of horizontally sheared stratified flow
Direct numerical simulations at low Froude number and high Reynolds number
Comparison of two instability-to-mixing pathways across buoyancy Reynolds number and vertical-scale content
evidence_signal: The abstract reports combined linear theory and direct numerical simulations showing two distinct transition pathways and comparing their resulting vertical scales and peak mixing efficiencies.
watch_item: The mixing pathway and efficiency depend on sufficiently large buoyancy Reynolds number, so the results may not transfer directly to lower-Re_b or less strongly stratified regimes.
paper_title: Two pathways to diapycnal mixing in strongly stratified flows with no initial vertical shear
